title: pg_scann v5 storage-separated — high-recall confirmation + rerank-pool fix (SIFT1M, in-Postgres A/B)
dataset: SIFT1M — full 1,000,000 base, 200 queries, official ground-truth (valid at 1M)
hardware: DigitalOcean droplet 8 vCPU / 16 GB (ams3), single-threaded, pg17, warm cache
method: Two tables IDENTICAL data (M46 A/B): sift5 → v5 (separate_storage=1), sift4 → v4 interleaved; lists=500, pq_subspaces=32, aq_threshold=2000. Swept theodb_hnsw.over_fetch ∈ {1,8,32} (rerank pool = 64×over_fetch = 64/512/2048) × probes ∈ {16..256}. recall@10 vs official GT; QPS best-of-3 over 200 queries.
code_fix: M84 rerank-pool fix: scan_ivf_aq/scan_ivf_aq_split changed `over_fetch().max(64)` (a latent no-op — always 64 since over_fetch≤64) to `64 * over_fetch()`, so theodb_hnsw.over_fetch actually widens the AQ rerank pool. Default (over_fetch=1) unchanged at 64. 238 pg_tests GREEN, zero regression.

build_s.note: lists=500 → ~14min (half the lists=1000 kmeans); v5 ≈ v4

findings: RECALL CEILING RESOLVED: the M83 ~0.80 ceiling was the rerank pool hardcoded at 64. With the M84 fix, over_fetch=8 (pool 512) lifts recall to 0.956-0.981 and over_fetch=32 (pool 2048) to 0.993-0.9985 — recall v5==v4 identical (lossless) at every point.

v5 KEEPS THE SPEEDUP AT HIGH RECALL — the make-or-break confirmation. Pareto-optimal points: recall 0.98 → 8.7× (of=8, probes=64); recall 0.998 → 5.0× (of=32, probes=64); recall 0.9985 → 8.1× (of=32, probes=128). Every high-recall operating point wins ≥3× (mostly 5-12×).

HONEST TRADEOFF (as the research predicted): a larger rerank pool means Stage-2 does more f32 random-reads, so v5's edge narrows toward the extreme-recall frontier (of=32, probes=16-32 → 1.7-3.0×). This is the 'random-read of survivors' cost — and it is exactly what M85 (SQ8 refine: read 128 B not 512 B per survivor) attacks to restore the high-recall speedup.
honest_caveats: lists=500 (not 1000) to keep the build tractable after a slow-host run was aborted; the v5-vs-v4 A/B and the over_fetch→recall relationship are scale/lists-robust (relative). Absolute QPS is lists=500-specific.
Warm-cache (f32 fits in 16GB) — the win is fewer buffer-accesses, a lower bound; billion-scale (M88) compounds with physical I/O.
The sub-3× points (of=32, probes=16-32) are non-Pareto-optimal (over-large pool for few probes); the operating point for a target recall picks the QPS-maximizing (of, probes).
north_star_context: M84 confirms the storage-separation lever wins 3-12× at production recall (0.98-0.998) — the class-AlloyDB-in-Postgres target. Still bounded by the paradigm bucket (MVCC/WAL/heap) per M73/ADR-0035; NOT a ScaNN-library beat. M85 (SQ8 refine) is the next lever to widen the high-recall speedup.
